\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{قابلمه} (qâblame)}{قابلمه (qâblame)}]{\fa{قابلمه} (qâblame) — a cooking pot, a saucepan}

\label{lesson:FA-C358-qablame}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for yeast, then the Persian for a clay oven.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{قابلمه}}
\textbf{\fa{قابلمه}} (\emph{qâblame}) — \textquotedblleft{}a cooking pot, a saucepan\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{آب} \fa{را} \fa{در} \fa{قابلمه} \fa{ریخت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Âb râ dar qâblame rikht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She poured the water into the pot.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{qâblame-hâ}. The lid is \emph{dar-e qâblame}.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \emph{qâblame} \textquotedblleft{}a cooking pot\textquotedblright{} is not settled, and EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{جوش} \fa{آمدن} (jush âmadan)}{جوش آمدن (jush âmadan)}]{\fa{جوش} \fa{آمدن} (jush âmadan) — to come to the boil}

\label{lesson:FA-C358-jush-amadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a clay oven, then the Persian for a cooking pot.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{جوش} \fa{آمدن}}
\textbf{\fa{جوش} \fa{آمدن}} (\emph{jush âmadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to come to the boil\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{وقتی} \fa{آب} \fa{جوش} \fa{آمد،} \fa{برنج} \fa{را} \fa{در} \fa{آن} \fa{ریخت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Vaqti âb jush âmad, berenj râ dar ân rikht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When the water came to the boil, she put the rice in.
\end{quote}

In speech also \textquotedblleft{}to lose one's temper\textquotedblright{}. Present \emph{jush miâyad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{jush} \textquotedblleft{}boiling, a simmer\textquotedblright{} is a Persian word that EtymDB lists without a parent; \emph{âmadan} \textquotedblleft{}to come\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jush âmadan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{jush âmadan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a clay oven, then the Persian for a cooking pot, then say \emph{jush âmadan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{قل} \fa{زدن} (qol zadan)}{قل زدن (qol zadan)}]{\fa{قل} \fa{زدن} (qol zadan) — to bubble, to simmer}

\label{lesson:FA-C358-qol-zadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a cooking pot, then the Persian for to come to the boil.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{قل} \fa{زدن}}
\textbf{\fa{قل} \fa{زدن}} (\emph{qol zadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to bubble, to simmer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{خورش} \fa{آرام} \fa{قل} \fa{میزد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Khoresh ârâm qol mizad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The stew was simmering gently.
\end{quote}

\emph{Qol} imitates the sound of bubbling. Present \emph{qol mizanad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{qol} is a sound-word that imitates bubbling; \emph{zadan} \textquotedblleft{}to strike\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian. EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{جا} \fa{افتادن} (jâ oftâdan)}{جا افتادن (jâ oftâdan)}]{\fa{جا} \fa{افتادن} (jâ oftâdan) — to be well cooked (of a stew); to settle in}

\label{lesson:FA-C358-ja-oftadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to come to the boil, then the Persian for to bubble.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{جا} \fa{افتادن}}
\textbf{\fa{جا} \fa{افتادن}} (\emph{jâ oftâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to be well cooked (of a stew); to settle in\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{خورش} \fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{دو} \fa{ساعت} \fa{جا} \fa{افتاد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Khoresh ba'd az do sâ'at jâ oftâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After two hours the stew was nicely cooked.
\end{quote}

Of a stew, the flavours have come together. Of a bone, \textquotedblleft{}to go back into place\textquotedblright{}; of an idea, \textquotedblleft{}to be accepted\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{jâ} \textquotedblleft{}place\textquotedblright{} is inherited from Middle Persian (EtymDB), and \emph{oftâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to fall\textquotedblright{} is native Persian: to fall into place.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کفگیر} (kafgir)}{کفگیر (kafgir)}]{\fa{کفگیر} (kafgir) — a slotted spoon, a skimmer}

\label{lesson:FA-C358-kafgir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to bubble, then the Persian for to be well cooked.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کفگیر}}
\textbf{\fa{کفگیر}} (\emph{kafgir}) — \textquotedblleft{}a slotted spoon, a skimmer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{برنج} \fa{را} \fa{با} \fa{کفگیر} \fa{در} \fa{بشقاب} \fa{کشید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Berenj râ bâ kafgir dar boshqâb keshid.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She served the rice onto the plate with a skimmer.
\end{quote}

\emph{kaf} \textquotedblleft{}foam\textquotedblright{} + \emph{gir} \textquotedblleft{}taker\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Kafgir be tah-e dig khord}, \textquotedblleft{}the skimmer hit the bottom of the pot\textquotedblright{}: nothing is left.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kafgir} joins \emph{kaf} \textquotedblleft{}foam\textquotedblright{} and \emph{gir-}, the present stem of \emph{gereftan} \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{}: the foam-taker. EtymDB lists the word without a parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
